report.summary: Outbox publications lagged arrivals for ~100 s (backlog up to 124, oldest age 38.5 s), then caught up. Deliveries succeeded; slow consumer handler time (~460 ms) coincides with the throttled publish rate.

findings.claim: Outbox publishing fell behind committed arrivals, building a backlog of up to 124 and oldest undelivered age of 38.5 s, then drained.
findings.reason: Arrivals were steady at 32/10s while publications dropped to 15-19/10s mid-window, then spiked to 80/10s; pending peaked at 124.

findings.claim: The consumer handler adds about 460 ms to some deliveries, raising total delivery time from ~71 ms to ~530 ms.
findings.reason: Handler p95 is 460 ms against a p50 of 0.022 ms; slow attempts in the logs are about 528-532 ms.

findings.claim: The reduced publish rate is consistent with serial delivery in batches polled every 1 s, where slow consumer responses cap throughput below the 3.2/s arrival rate.
findings.reason: Slow attempts of ~0.5 s on a 1 s poll interval would limit throughput to about 1.7/s, matching the ~17 per 10 s buckets. Serial delivery itself is not directly observed.

limitations: The 100 delivery log rows listed cover only the first ~33 s, so the slow period is not shown in individual records.
Consumer timings come from a test fixture and may not reflect a real consumer; the cause of the consumer's slowness is unknown.
